objective: Using a specific instance where clean laundry did not make it into its storage spot correctly, learners diagnose the break in their put-away system with an adult and adjust the system so it works next time.
scenario: The learner looks at a real, current example of laundry that didn't make it fully into its system — a basket of clean clothes sitting for days, an item in the wrong drawer — and works with an adult to figure out exactly where the system broke down before fixing both the immediate pile and the underlying system.
safetyNotes: No shame language is used toward whoever the pile belongs to.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no current backlog of unstored laundry to diagnose, the learner instead reviews a short written scenario describing someone else's stalled put-away system, identifies the likely sticking-point step, and proposes a specific fix the same way as the guided task.

materials: the actual current pile of clean laundry

tasks.directions: Describe the specific put-away problem you're looking at right now — not 'my laundry system doesn't work' but exactly what's out of place.
With your adult, trace back: at what step did this pile stop moving toward its storage spot?

prompts.text: I named the exact step where the system stopped (washed but not folded, folded but not carried to its room, carried but not put in the drawer, etc.).
My adult and I agreed on one specific reason that step is the sticking point.
We named one small change to the system, not just 'try harder.'

tasks.directions: Put away the current pile correctly, then test your one system change by doing it again with a second small batch.

prompts.text: Did the system change work the second time? What did you notice?
Explain your updated put-away system in your own words, from clean-and-dry to fully stored, and name the one step you'll watch most closely next time.

remediation: If the learner's proposed fix is vague ('I'll remember next time'), reteach by having them name a specific trigger — a time of day, a location, or a linked habit — that will cue the sticking-point step, then test that trigger with a small batch.
extension: Apply the same diagnose-and-fix process to a different put-away system in the home (dishes, school supplies, toys) and compare whether the same sticking-point step shows up there too.
